etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Middle English determinate, determynat, determinat, from Latin dēterminātus, perfect passive participle of dēterminō (“to limit, set bounds”), see -ate (adjective-forming suffix) for more.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
paragraphs: From a substantivation of the above adjective. See -ate (noun-forming suffix) for more.
senses: (philosophy) A single state of a particular determinable attribute.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English determinaten, from determinat +‎ -en, see Etymology 1 and -ate (verb-forming suffix) for more. Compare French déterminer.
senses: (obsolete) To bring to an end; to determine.
